clue.text: Concentrate on studies in college 'after vacation

indicators.note: in places the run of letters for 'on studies' inside the emptied college
a vacated college has been emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
dens are studies, private rooms for work

explanation.surface: A student is urged to focus on study once back at college after the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after vacation' sounds like the end of term, but it means emptying the word 'college' down to its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To concentrate a liquid or an argument is to make it denser and shorter, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Type of bend' in length of old painter

indicators.note: in means the bend letter is placed inside the old length

parts.note: a cubit is an ancient measure of length, from elbow to fingertip
an S-bend is a type of bend in a pipe or road

explanation.surface: Someone asks what kind of bend appears in an old painter's lengths.
explanation.walkthrough: An S-bend is a U-shaped trap in a drain pipe or a bend in a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cubist is a painter of the Cubism school, like Picasso or Braque.

clue.text: Close, as found in Newbolt?

parts.note: the name is split as New + bolt; N is the standard abbreviation for new
the bolt of Newbolt, a crossbow bolt, is an arrow

explanation.surface: A question of whether closeness is found in the poet Henry Newbolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Newbolt is the poet Henry Newbolt; the clue splits his name into NEW (N) and BOLT (ARROW).
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow victory or escape is a close one.

clue.text: Representation of character in passage

definitions.meaning: acting out a role on stage
the passing of a bill into law

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is acting a part on stage; the other is the passing of a law.

clue.text: One raising animals, possibly brockets (deer)

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged into another word

explanation.surface: A breeder of livestock might raise brockets, a kind of deer.
explanation.walkthrough: A brocket is a small South American deer; 'possibly' shuffles BROCKETS DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockbreeder rears farm animals, the livestock, for sale.

clue.text: In a period of prosperity, left out

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: In at the head of the clue tells us the next item is placed inside what follows

parts.note: a boom is a time of economic prosperity

explanation.surface: Someone feels excluded during a time of wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'left out' but stands alone as the definition: flowers that are out are in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that are out are open and blossoming, the same state as being in bloom.

clue.text: Supports second front

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments

explanation.surface: Underwear gives support to the second front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' looks military but means nerve: 'brass neck' is British for cheek or effrontery.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass and front both mean cheek or impudence, as in a brass neck.

clue.text: Excursion taking in game and departing

indicators.note: taking in means the outing word holds the game word inside

parts.note: an outing is a short trip or excursion
go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A day trip includes a game and then a departure.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoing means leaving office or departing, as an outgoing president.

clue.text: Poet most needed when one fellow turns up for burial?

indicators.note: for burial means the reversed letters are buried inside the word most
in a down clue, turns up means the letters run upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A poet is most needed when a colleague arrives for a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: I DON read upwards gives NODI, buried in MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: A monodist writes monodies, mourning poems for a single voice, so is a poet.

clue.text: Changing green, initially, to amber' or orange?

indicators.note: Changing tells us the letters that follow are rearranged into a new order
initially picks the first letter of green

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Traffic lights going from green to amber, or perhaps orange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes G from 'green'; 'Changing' shuffles G with TO AMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: The bergamot is a citrus fruit, a kind of sour orange whose rind yields an oil used in Earl Grey tea.

clue.text: Not this clue? Return to printer

indicators.note: Return tells us the run of letters built from the clue words is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
this clue is 10 across, written in Roman numerals and abbreviation as X AC

explanation.surface: A puzzle note telling the solver to go back to the printer, not this clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this clue' refers to the clue's own label, 10 across: X (Roman ten) plus AC (across). NOT XAC read backwards gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: William Caxton set up the first printing press in England in the 1470s.

clue.text: Quote Minister endlessly floundering -. that's regular in the House

indicators.note: floundering means the letters struggle about and fall into a new order
endlessly means the last letter of minister is lopped off

explanation.surface: A minister flounders when quoted at a regular parliamentary session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the R from MINISTER; 'floundering' shuffles QUOTE MINISTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Question time is a regular session in Parliament where ministers answer members' questions.

clue.text: Rapid fire

definitions.meaning: a stretch of fast-flowing water, a rapid in a river
to fire a gun is to discharge it at a target

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a rush of fast water in a river; the other is to discharge a weapon.

clue.text: Town reeked going west to river crossing

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means the word is written right to left

parts.note: stunk is a past tense of stink, so reeked
a ford is a shallow place to cross a river

explanation.surface: A smelly town that drifts west towards a ford.
explanation.walkthrough: KNUTSFORD is a market town in Cheshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Knutsford is a market town in Cheshire in north-west England.

clue.text: This stranger moved the affections

indicators.note: moved tells us the letters of the words before it are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A stranger touched someone's emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' looks like the emotional verb of the surface but is the anagram signal on THIS STRANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartstrings are a person's deepest feelings, the seat of love and pity, so they are the affections.

clue.text: Cancelled — as result of end of fair spell

definitions.meaning: called off, as a match or fete

definitions.text: as result of end of fair spell
definitions.meaning: a spell of fine weather ending and wet weather stopping an event

explanation.definitionFit: Both readings describe an outdoor event called off because of rain after fine weather.

clue.text: Small animals scatter as grass is disturbed

parts.note: moles are small burrowing animals
to ted is to spread mown grass out to dry for hay

explanation.surface: Moles scatter as the lawn is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: To ted hay is an old farming word: to spread cut grass to dry.
explanation.definitionFit: To molest someone is to pester or harass them, so molested means disturbed or bothered.

clue.text: This said, one's about to perform, say, among lions.

definitions.text: This said, one's about to perform

indicators.note: among means the next letters sit inside the word for lions

parts.note: lions are heroes, celebrated brave people
eg, for example, is often signalled by say

explanation.surface: A lion tamer is about to perform among lions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lions' looks like big cats but means celebrities or heroes.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer about to begin says this phrase to brace for an attempt.

clue.text: Speeding — and with one too many?.

definitions.meaning: driving faster than the legal limit allows
having had one drink too many, so drunk beyond the legal amount for driving

explanation.definitionFit: Both readings describe exceeding a legal maximum, one for road speed and one for blood alcohol.

clue.text: Time over check-up about one minute? Even less!

indicators.note: about means the time and check letters are placed round the letter for one
in a down clue, over means the time letter sits on top of what follows
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A doctor's check-up runs over time by about one minute.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts T on top and 'up' turns the check word round; 'about' then wraps that run round the letter for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinier is the comparative of tiny, so it means even more minute.

clue.text: Distinguishing Mark, Rex and Harry

parts.note: a badge is a distinguishing mark or emblem
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A list of three men's names: Mark, Rex and Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark, Rex and Harry' looks like three names; Harry is a verb meaning harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger and to harry both mean to pester someone persistently.

clue.text: Being fresh, work on in flat

indicators.note: in tells us the work-on letters sit inside the word for flat

parts.note: flat ground is level or even
the erg is a unit of work in physics
re means on or about, as in a business letter

explanation.surface: Someone stays fresh by working on in a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home, but here it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evergreen keeps its freshness and never seems to age, like a plant that keeps its leaves.

clue.text: Bishop breaks into song in church grounds

indicators.note: breaks into means the bishop letter enters the song word

parts.note: a glee is a part-song for unaccompanied voices
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop bursts into song in the churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Glebe is land belonging to a parish church, providing income for the vicar.

clue.text: Rejected land measure to protect one heath

indicators.note: to protect means the reversed measure is wrapped round the next letter
Rejected means the word for the land measure is turned back to front

parts.note: an acre is a unit of land area
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An area of moorland is turned down for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns ACRE into ERCA, which wraps round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers.

clue.text: Gardening tool to put some pile-worts back

indicators.note: back means the run of letters is read in reverse order
some tells us only part of the letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A gardener needs a tool to replant pilewort, a wild flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Pilewort is the lesser celandine; 'some' takes LEWORT from it and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool with a pointed scoop, used in gardening for planting.

clue.text: Taking the controls? Can, 'with good flying record all round

parts.note: pi, short for pious, is crosswordese for good

indicators.note: all round means the log letters surround the word for can

parts.note: a log is a record of flights, as in a pilot's logbook
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a pilot with a good flight record can take control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb but is the container; the word for good comes first even though the clue gives it later.
explanation.definitionFit: Piloting an aircraft means being at the controls and steering it.

clue.text: Person removing dirty coat, one in 50's style

definitions.meaning: someone who wipes away a grimy layer of dust from surfaces
a long light coat fashionable in the 1950s

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a cleaner who wipes dust away; the other is a loose light overcoat popular in the 1950s.

clue.text: Voyager a long way off picked up by observer

indicators.note: picked up by means the letters are held inside the word for observer

parts.note: a seer is one who sees, an observer
taken as written
far means a long way off

explanation.surface: A traveller far away is spotted by a watcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer travels by sea, so is a voyager.
